_meta.indication: NULIBRY is indicated to reduce the risk of mortality in patients with molybdenum cofactor deficiency (MoCD) Type A.

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Combined analysis of Studies MCD-501, MCD-201, and MCD-202 (treated cohort) versus untreated natural history control (Study MCD-502)
pivotal_trials.phase: Phase 2 (Study MCD-201); efficacy derived from pooled clinical trials plus a retrospective observational study and a natural history control
pivotal_trials.design: Nonrandomized, uncontrolled, open-label treated cohort pooled from two clinical trials and a retrospective observational study, compared to a matched untreated external (natural history) control cohort
pivotal_trials.population: Neonatal and pediatric patients with genetically confirmed MoCD Type A
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Overall survival, comparing the treated group to an untreated natural history control cohort
pivotal_trials.n: 13 treated patients versus 18 genotype-matched untreated (GMAS) controls (and 37 untreated in the FAS)
pivotal_trials.result: 2 (15.4%) deaths in fosdenopterin group vs 12 (66.7%) in untreated GMAS; unadjusted Cox HR 0.18 (Lin et al. 95% CI 0.04, 0.71); log-rank p=0.0121; 3-year KM survival 84% vs 55%

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>25%): catheter-related complications (89%), pyrexia (78%), viral infection (56%), pneumonia (44%), otitis media (44%), vomiting (44%), cough/sneezing (44%), gastroenteritis (33%), diarrhea (33%), bacteremia (33%). Potential for photosensitivity based on nonclinical phototoxicity.
target_moa: Fosdenopterin is a chemically synthesized form of cyclic pyranopterin monophosphate (cPMP) that provides an exogenous source of cPMP; cPMP is converted to molybdopterin and then to molybdenum cofactor (MoCo), restoring MoCo biosynthesis (deficient in MoCD Type A due to MOCS1 mutations) and thereby MoCo-dependent enzyme activity such as sulfite oxidase.
modality: Small molecule (chemically synthesized cyclic pyranopterin monophosphate; substrate replacement therapy)
companion_dx_detail: No companion diagnostic; genetic testing confirms MoCD Type A but no FDA-cleared companion test is required. Start if known or presumed MoCD Type A; promptly discontinue if not confirmed by genetic testing.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened; FDA did not identify efficacy or safety issues needing external input.

basis.text: Review classification was priority because fosdenopterin is a drug for a serious disease with no approved therapy that would provide a significant advance.

citations.quote: The Division determined that the review classification for NDA 214018 was priority because fosdenopterin is a drug for a serious disease with no approved therapy, and if approved, fosdenopterin would provide a significant advance.

summary.text: NDA 214018 received priority review for a serious disease with no approved therapy; the drug had Orphan Drug Designation (Nov 5, 2009), Breakthrough Therapy Designation (Oct 23, 2013), and Rare Pediatric Disease Designation (Jun 15, 2017). This was a traditional (not accelerated) approval, approved February 26, 2021 on the first cycle without an advisory committee.
